Citation index and ranking

Source: R/citation_rank.R
citation_rank.Rd

Ranks papers (or venues, or authors) by citation count and computes summary citation indices (h-index, g-index, i10-index and more) for the whole collection. Written in base R, so it adds no package dependencies.

Usage

citation_rank(
  data,
  by = c("paper", "venue", "author"),
  cites = "cited_by",
  year = "year",
  title = "title",
  venue = "venue",
  authors = "authors",
  sep = "\\s+and\\s+",
  current_year = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")),
  na_cites_as_zero = TRUE,
  drop_untitled = TRUE,
  dedupe = TRUE,
  top_n = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per paper, such as the result of [scholar_parse_html()] or [bib_to_df()].

by

What to rank: `"paper"` (default), `"venue"` or `"author"`. For `"author"`, each author is credited with the full citation count of every paper they appear on.

cites, year, title, venue, authors

Names of the columns in `data`. Defaults match the Google Scholar layout. If there is no `authors` column but there is an `author` column (as from [bib_to_df()]), that one is used.

sep

Regular expression separating authors. Default `"\s+and\s+"`.

current_year

Year used to compute paper age. Defaults to this year.

na_cites_as_zero

If `TRUE` (default), a missing citation count is treated as 0, which is how Google Scholar reports an uncited paper (no "Cited by" link). If `FALSE`, those rows are dropped.

drop_untitled

If `TRUE` (default), rows with no title (usually parse failures) are dropped with a message.

dedupe

If `TRUE` (default), remove duplicate listings of the same paper before counting (see [find_duplicate_papers()]): the less-cited copy is dropped, a message names the rows, and they are returned in `$duplicates`. Use `FALSE` to count every row.

top_n

Optional. Keep only the top `n` rows of the ranked table. Indices are always computed on the full data.

Value

An object of class `citelens_rank`, a list with:

ranked

Data frame sorted by rank. For `by = "paper"`: `rank`, `title`, `authors`, `venue`, `year`, `citations`, `percentile`, `share`, `cum_share`, `age`, `cites_per_year`, `rank_per_year`. For `"venue"` and `"author"`: `rank`, the entity name, `n_papers`, `total_citations`, `mean_citations`, `max_citations`, `h_index`, `share`, `cum_share`.

index

One-row data frame of whole-collection indices: `n_papers`, `total`, `mean`, `median`, `max`, `uncited`, `h_index`, `g_index`, `i10_index`.

by, n_total

What was ranked, and the number of rows before `top_n`.

duplicates

Rows dropped as duplicate listings, or `NULL`.

Details

* **h-index**: the largest h such that h papers each have at least h citations. * **g-index**: the largest g such that the top g papers together have at least g^2 citations (capped at the number of papers). * **i10-index**: number of papers with at least 10 citations. * **rank** uses competition ranking (`ties.method = "min"`), so tied papers share a rank and the next rank is skipped. * **percentile** is the percent of papers with strictly fewer citations. * **cites_per_year** is citations divided by the paper's age, where age = `current_year - year + 1`, so a paper from this year has age 1.

Author and venue tables are built from the papers that remain after de-duplication and cleaning.

See also

[find_duplicate_papers()], [author_network()]

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "sample_authors.csv", package = "citelens")
d <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
res <- citation_rank(d, current_year = 2024)
#> Dropped 1 duplicate paper listing(s): row 7. Use dedupe = FALSE to keep them; see $duplicates.
res
